back: The minimum payment needed to keep a factor in its present use: its opportunity cost (the earnings in its next best use).
The surplus paid to a factor over its transfer earnings: actual payment minus transfer earnings.
Economic rent = actual earnings − transfer earnings.

front: On a supply and demand diagram, where are rent and transfer earnings?
back: Rent: the area above the supply curve and below the price. Transfer earnings: the area under the supply curve up to the quantity.
All of the factor's earnings are economic rent (transfer earnings are zero).
All of the factor's earnings are transfer earnings; there is no economic rent.
A temporary surplus on a factor fixed in the short run (revenue minus variable costs) that disappears in the long run.

front: Why may a tax on economic rent not reduce supply?
back: The after-tax payment is still above the factor's transfer earnings, so it stays in its use.

front: Why is the rent earned by a top footballer high?
back: Scarce talent with no close substitutes gives inelastic supply, while the next best job pays far less.
